rule.title: Permissionless function performs a swap-like economic action with no caller guard

intent.attack_thesis: A non-view function with no caller authorization triggers a swap-like operation on an AMM router (Uniswap/Pancake/Sushi V2/V3/Curve). The swap's parameters are caller-influenced (typical: a uint amount argument). Because the AMM swap moves the pool's spot price, an attacker can sandwich the call with a flash loan: borrow asset A, push the price, trigger the unguarded swap on the victim (forcing the victim to sell at a bad rate), arbitrage the now-skewed pool, repay the loan, and pocket the difference. This is the root pattern behind BurgerSwap, the BSC GPC/MSC drain, and many small-cap reward-distribution exploits.

reporting.title_template: Permissionless function triggers AMM swap — vulnerable to flash-loan price manipulation
reporting.summary: Matches non-view functions with no caller-authorization guard that reach a swap-like external call. An attacker can trigger the call permissionlessly and wrap it in a flash-loan sandwich to extract arbitrage profit from the resulting pool-price move.
reporting.user_summary: Anyone can call this function. The function performs a token swap on a DEX (Uniswap/Pancake/Sushi-style router). Because the swap moves the pool's price and there is no access control, an attacker can borrow funds via a flash loan, manipulate the pool price up or down, trigger this function so the contract trades at a bad rate, then arbitrage the difference and repay the loan in a single atomic transaction. The attacker walks away with the profit; the contract is drained of value.
reporting.technical_summary: The detector matches functions whose body contains a swap-like external call (UniV2/V3 routers, Curve exchange, Balancer batchSwap, or direct pair swap selectors) AND whose dispatch reaches that call without any authorized_path predicate firing — no caller==owner check, no role guard, no allowlist. SWAP_OR_LIQUIDITY_PATTERN must hold (the analyzer has resolved at least one swap-shape call site). The reachable_effect set must include asset_transfer or accounting_mutation, confirming value moves on the unguarded path. The verifier (anvil-fork-economic) provides the dynamic witness by replaying the call from an attacker EOA and observing the swap selector fire in the trace.
reporting.exploit_narrative: The attacker drafts an atomic exploit transaction: (1) flash-borrow a large amount of token A from Aave/Balancer/Uniswap; (2) swap A for B on the victim's AMM pair to push the price; (3) call the unguarded function on the victim contract — the contract swaps its own balance at the now-bad rate; (4) reverse the manipulation by swapping B back to A; (5) repay the flash loan plus fee; (6) keep the residual A as profit. Total cost: one block, one transaction, capped only by the size of the available flash loan.
exploit_preconditions: function has no caller==owner / role / allowlist guard
function reaches a call to a known DEX router / pair swap selector
the swap consumes attacker-influenced or contract-balance amounts
a tradeable AMM pair exists with non-trivial reserves the attacker can manipulate
remediation_hints: add an owner / role / allowlist guard (OZ Ownable, AccessControl, governance)

if the function is INTENDED to be permissionless, enforce slippage internally: compute expected output from an external oracle (Chainlink TWAP, Uniswap V3 TWAP) and revert if the actual is outside a tolerance band
rate-limit per-block or per-caller to bound MEV extraction even when the function is open
consider whether the function should exist at all — many 'releaseReward' / 'distribute' / 'rebalance' patterns should be admin-only crons rather than callable by anyone

preconditions: victim contract holds token balance the swap will consume
tradeable AMM pair exists with the token
flash-loan source is available on the chain (Aave / Balancer / Uniswap)

steps.expected_state: attacker holds the borrowed amount for the duration of the tx

steps.action: swap A for B on the AMM pair to push the price up by X%
steps.expected_state: pool reserves skewed; spot price moved

steps.action: call the unguarded function on the victim; victim swaps at the bad rate
steps.expected_state: victim spends value to obtain less than market value back

steps.action: swap B back to A to revert the price; repay the flash loan + fee
steps.expected_state: pool restored, loan repaid, residual A retained as profit

witness_goal.success_condition: attacker ends the transaction with more value than they started, paid for by the victim contract
environment_requirements: deployed victim contract with the unguarded function
